Why the file system resize? Just to make room for LUKS files?

Because, and this is new to me, the physical allocation and the ext4 filesystem don't have to be the same size.

The ext4, or whatever you're using, expect access to the whole area they've been allocated and you can write over the LUKS headers and never decrypt it.

It turns out that you can have a partition of size 40G and have an FS on it of 39G. Or in other words a LUKS partition always has to be a little bigger than the FS it represents. That would be true of LVM too.
